newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway budget surplus cd top target by 40pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Norway budget surplus cd top target by 40pct-paper.

text.p: Norway's budget surplus could run to 80 or 90 billion crowns in 1997, 40 percent higher than the government's forecast of 57.7 billion crowns in this year's final budget in May, the daily Finansavisen said on Thursday.
The estimate is double the government's original projection of 40.9 billion crowns in the draft budget in October.
Finansavisen said increased tax revenues and higher oil prices had contributed to the rise. A favourable dollar exchange rate against the crown had also helped bolster state coffers.
Norway, which produces around 3.2 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil and uses just 150,000 bpd, is the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.

Norwegian monetary policy is geared to keeping the crown at a stable exchange rate against a basket of European currencies, known as the inverse European Currency Unit (ECU) index, rather than against a trade-weighted exchange rate basket.
Finansavisen said that monetary policy and developments in the dollar exchange rate had led to a sharp increase in state revenues from oil activities.
Oil prices in the first half of the year averaged around 134 crowns per barrel and now stand at over 140 crowns per barrel following a rise in the dollar.
The government's estimate for the 1997 budget surplus in the final budget were based on an average oil price of 125 crowns.
